Rightor, E., Whitlock, A. and Elliott, R.N. (2020). Beneficial Electrification in Industry. Report IE2002. Washington, DC: American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy (ACEEE), July 2020. https://www.aceee.org/sites/default/files/pdfs/ie2002.pdf

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 5). A policy and opportunity report, not a technology data source: almost no unit-level numbers. Loaded: the applicable temperature range and development status of each electrotechnology in Table A1 (heat pumps below 90 degC and 90-160 degC, electric boilers and steam generators 100-150 degC, microwave/RF, ohmic, infrared, induction, resistance and UV with TRL where printed), the heat pump temperature capability of 120 degC (150 degC achievable) and a personal-communication seasonal CoP of 9.5-11 flagged as unverified. Sector statistics, the electric-boiler cost comparison (up to 40% below gas boiler), potentials and waste-heat figures are in other-values. Not loaded: figures 4-6 (process-heat distribution by temperature and industry, charts), electrolysis, CHP, refining and cement sections (no technology numbers), ultrasound, pulsed electric field, pulsed light and friction heating (Table A1 rows with TRL only, no archetype). Overlap: heat pump temperatures echo arpagaus_2018_001 and iea-hpt_2023_001, which hold the product-level data; Zuhlsdorf et al. (2019) is cited for 280 degC.

(1) Seasonal CoP 9.5-11 is attributed to a personal communication (Pears 2019) with no lift or conditions; it is inconsistent with published industrial heat pump COPs. (2) Table A1 gives TRL as ranges or "Commercial" only. (3) Electric boiler cost comparison is relative (no absolute cost) and uses 2015 prices.
